newsitem.title: UK: IPE says all obstacles cleared for natgas contract.
newsitem.headline: IPE says all obstacles cleared for natgas contract.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) said on Thursday that all the approvals are now in place for the launch of a natural gas forward contract, which could be up and running in January.

U.K. gas regulator Ofgas has approved the necessary modifications to the Network Code for the launch of the monthly contract based at the National Balancing Point (NBP), said IPE director of business development Richard Ward.
The IPE board and the board of the London Clearing House (LCH) have also given their go-ahead for the launch.
"All our ducks are in a row," said Ward.
Last week an IPE official said the contract launch was likely to follow about six to eight weeks after the approvals were given.
"Sometime in January sounds about right. We're not talking Christmas," Ward said.
Modification to the Network Code -- the rulebook for shippers -- was required for the LCH to gain access to the A.T. Link screen system which shows trade nominations at the NBP.
In its initial form, the NBP contract will offer only monthly trading for 12 months ahead.
"We wanted to launch something simple," said an IPE official. "When the industry asks for day-ahead to start we will ask for LCH approval."
